article.title: From Prediction to Intervention: Why the Highest-Score Customers May Not Be the Best Targets
article.why: Distinguish propensity from incremental impact when making targeting decisions.

paragraphs.en:
Propensity models are attractive because they rank customers by the probability of an outcome: buying insurance, responding to an offer, renewing a subscription, or using a service. A natural targeting rule is therefore to contact the customers with the highest scores. Yet this rule can be economically inefficient. The customers most likely to buy are not necessarily the customers whose behavior is most likely to change because of the campaign.

Consider two customers. Customer A has an 80 percent probability of purchasing even without a message. A campaign raises that probability to 82 percent. Customer B has only a 20 percent baseline probability, but a well-designed message raises it to 30 percent. A conventional propensity model will rank A above B because 82 percent is greater than 30 percent. From an intervention perspective, however, B is more valuable: the incremental effect is ten percentage points rather than two.

This distinction separates prediction from causal decision-making. Prediction asks what is likely to happen. Targeting asks what will happen differently if we take an action. The relevant quantity is often called uplift, incremental treatment effect, or conditional average treatment effect. Estimating it is harder than estimating propensity because we never observe the same customer both treated and untreated at the same moment. Randomized experiments provide the cleanest foundation, while observational approaches require stronger assumptions about confounding and treatment assignment.

High-propensity customers can include ‘sure things’: people who would convert anyway. Spending campaign budget on them may produce impressive observed conversion rates without producing much incremental value. At the opposite extreme are ‘lost causes,’ customers unlikely to convert even with treatment. Between these groups may be persuadable customers whose outcome is genuinely sensitive to the intervention. There can even be customers for whom treatment has a negative effect, for example because excessive messaging creates annoyance or distrust.

This does not mean propensity models are useless. They can still support prioritization when randomized treatment data are unavailable, and they may help define eligible populations or operational capacity. But decision-makers should be precise about what the score represents. A probability of conversion is not a probability of being persuaded. The distinction becomes especially important when contact has a cost, when channels have limited capacity, or when over-contact creates customer harm.

Economics adds another layer. Even uplift is not the final objective if customers have different expected values or treatment costs. A useful targeting score may combine incremental probability with expected margin, contact cost, risk, and capacity constraints. For example, a five-percentage-point uplift on a high-value product may be worth more than a ten-point uplift on a low-margin product. Likewise, an intervention that works well but requires an expensive human call may be less attractive than a smaller effect delivered through a low-cost digital channel.

Evaluation must also match the decision problem. A model can have excellent discrimination or calibration and still be poor for intervention targeting. For uplift models, teams may examine treatment-effect heterogeneity, uplift or gain curves, policy value, and randomized holdout performance. Most importantly, the evaluation should ask whether selecting customers with the model creates more incremental business value than a reasonable alternative policy.

A practical organization can move gradually. Start with a propensity model if that is the available infrastructure, but preserve randomized control groups in campaigns. Accumulate treatment and outcome data. Compare conversion among treated and control customers within score bands. If high-score bands show high conversion but little treatment-control difference, the model is identifying likely buyers rather than persuadable buyers. That evidence can motivate an uplift or causal targeting approach.

The conceptual shift is simple but powerful: do not ask only, ‘Who is most likely to buy?’ Ask, ‘Whose outcome can we improve by acting, and is the improvement worth the cost?’ Once targeting is framed this way, prediction becomes one input to a decision rather than the decision itself.
paragraphs.zh:
Propensity model 會依購買、回應、續約或使用服務的機率排序顧客，因此直覺做法是優先接觸最高分者。但這可能在經濟上沒有效率：最可能購買的人，不一定是最會因 campaign 而改變行為的人。

例如 A 即使不收到訊息也有80%購買率，施策後升到82%；B 的 baseline 只有20%，但訊息可提升到30%。傳統 propensity 會把 A 排在 B 前面，但從 intervention 角度，B 的 incremental effect 是10個百分點，遠高於 A 的2點。

這就是 prediction 與 causal decision-making 的差異。Prediction 問「什麼最可能發生」，targeting 問「採取行動後，什麼會因此不同」。關鍵量常稱 uplift、incremental treatment effect 或 CATE。它比 propensity 難估，因為同一顧客同一時刻無法同時觀察 treated 與 untreated 結果；randomized experiment 是最乾淨的基礎，observational 方法則需要更強的 confounding 假設。

高 propensity 群可能包含本來就會買的 sure things；對他們花預算會讓 observed conversion 很漂亮，卻不一定創造多少增量價值。另一端則是施策也不會買的 lost causes。真正有價值的可能是介於中間、會被施策改變的 persuadable customers，甚至還可能存在因過度訊息而反感的負向 treatment effect。

這不代表 propensity 無用。在沒有 randomized treatment data 時仍可用於優先排序、eligibility 或 capacity 管理，但必須清楚 score 的含義：conversion probability 並不是 persuasion probability。當接觸有成本、渠道容量有限或過度接觸會傷害顧客時尤其重要。

經濟性還要再加一層。即使 uplift 高，若顧客價值與 treatment cost 不同，也未必是最終最優。targeting score 可進一步結合 incremental probability、expected margin、contact cost、risk 與 capacity constraint。

評估方式也要對齊決策問題。discrimination 或 calibration 很好的模型，仍可能不適合 intervention targeting。Uplift model 可看 treatment-effect heterogeneity、uplift/gain curve、policy value 與 randomized holdout。核心問題是：用模型選人是否比合理的替代 policy 創造更多 incremental business value。

實務上可漸進轉型：先保留現有 propensity model，但 campaign 中持續保留 randomized control group，累積 treatment 與 outcome data，並在各 score band 比較 treated-control 差異。若高分群 conversion 很高但兩組差異很小，就表示模型主要找到「本來就會買的人」，這會成為導入 uplift/causal targeting 的證據。

觀念上的轉換很簡單：不要只問「誰最可能買？」而要問「對誰採取行動能改善 outcome，而且改善值得成本嗎？」如此 prediction 就只是決策的一個 input，而不是決策本身。
paragraphs.ja:
Propensity modelは購入、反応、更新などの確率で顧客をrank付けするため、最高score層から接触するのが自然に見えます。しかし最も買いそうな顧客が、campaignによって最も行動を変える顧客とは限りません。

例えばAはmessageなしでも80％で購入し、施策後82％。Bはbaseline 20％ですが施策後30％になるとします。propensityではAが上位ですが、interventionのincremental effectはAが2pt、Bが10ptなのでBの方が価値があります。

predictionは「何が起きそうか」を問い、targetingは「行動を取ることで何が変わるか」を問います。後者の量はuplift、incremental treatment effect、CATEなどと呼ばれます。同一顧客のtreated/untreated結果を同時観測できないため推定は難しく、randomized experimentが最も強い基盤になります。

高propensity層には施策なしでも買うsure thingsが含まれます。そこへ予算を使えばobserved conversionは高く見えてもincremental valueは小さい。一方、施策しても動かないlost causesもいます。その間に施策で本当に動くpersuadable customersがおり、過剰接触で逆効果になる顧客も存在し得ます。

propensity modelが不要という意味ではありません。randomized dataがなければ優先順位、eligibility、capacity管理に使えます。ただしconversion probabilityとpersuasion probabilityは別物です。接触costやchannel capacity、過剰接触riskがあるほど区別が重要です。

さらにupliftだけでなく経済価値も考えます。incremental probabilityにexpected margin、contact cost、risk、capacity constraintを組み合わせると、よりdecision-orientedなscoreになります。高価値商品の5pt upliftが低margin商品の10pt upliftより価値を持つ場合もあります。

評価もdecision problemに合わせます。discriminationやcalibrationが優秀でもintervention targetingには弱いことがあります。uplift/gain curve、treatment-effect heterogeneity、policy value、randomized holdoutなどを見て、model policyが代替policyよりincremental business valueを生むか確認します。

実務では既存propensityから段階的に移行できます。campaignでrandomized controlを残し、treatmentとoutcomeを蓄積し、score band別にtreated-control差を比較します。高score帯のconversionは高いのに差が小さければ、「買いそうな人」は捉えても「動かせる人」は捉えていない証拠になります。

最終的には「誰が買いそうか」だけでなく「誰に働きかければoutcomeを改善でき、その改善はcostに見合うか」と問います。predictionはdecisionそのものではなく、decisionへのinputになります。
